excerpt: PeakRoutine is an iPhone health coach that links sleep, HRV, daylight, mood and nutrition data from Apple Health and builds habits around them.
content:
PeakRoutine is an iPhone app that reads your health data through Apple Health, so data from an Apple Watch, Oura, WHOOP or similar devices flows in on its own. It looks for links between your sleep, heart-rate variability (HRV), daylight exposure, exercise, nutrition, mood and hydration, and explains what they mean for you. Six AI coaches (health, sleep, fitness, nutrition, recovery and mental health) answer questions using your own data, and a habit engine builds a daily plan that adjusts to how recovered you are.

The makers say it is a wellness app, not a clinical tool for diagnosing or managing a condition. Its site says it is free to start, that subscriptions can be cancelled any time in the app or the App Store, and that your data is never sold or shared with advertisers.

PeakRoutine was started by co-founders Siddhant Gupta and Sakshi Khare. Siddhant writes on its About page that a pre-diabetes diagnosis, and wearable data that never explained why, led him to build it. It launched on Product Hunt on 16 June 2026 and finished #4 for the day with 266 upvotes and 47 comments (as of 14 October 2026).

We have not tested PeakRoutine ourselves. This page brings together its official site, its Product Hunt launch and the public pages of comparable apps, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.os: iOS; reads data through Apple Health
profile.starts_at: Free to start; subscription prices not published on its site
profile.summary_short: AI health coach that connects your wearable and lifestyle data and builds habits around it

gallery.alt: PeakRoutine graphic 'Personalized health coaching powered by your biomarkers' with a phone showing an activity score of 81 and active habits
Two PeakRoutine screens titled 'Deep dives on sleep and daylight': a sleep-stage chart and a daylight exposure curve with sun habits
PeakRoutine's six AI coaches: health, sleep, fitness, nutrition, recovery and mental health
PeakRoutine chats with the Recovery Coach ('Why am I so tired today?') and the Fitness Coach ('Can I push hard today?') answering from HRV, sleep and heart-rate data

paragraphs: Siddhant Gupta says he was pre-diabetic at 32 with an Apple Watch full of data and still no idea what was making him unwell; it turned out to be his sleep, and no app had told him. He calls most health apps expensive mirrors that track everything and change nothing.

PeakRoutine was built to close that gap: it pulls in sleep, sunlight, exercise, nutrition, mood, hydration, HRV and stress through Apple Health, looks for patterns specific to you, and adds six AI coaches and a habit engine that builds a plan around your biology.
launch_story.attribution: Siddhant Gupta, co-founder, on Product Hunt

use_cases: Finding out which habit (sleep, daylight, exercise) is behind low energy or poor recovery
Getting a daily plan that eases off on low-recovery days
Asking an AI coach about sleep, HRV or nutrition with answers based on your own data
Seeing data from several wearables and apps in one place through Apple Health

fit: already wear an Apple Watch, Oura, WHOOP or similar and want the data explained
want habits and coaching, not just more charts
not_fit: need medical diagnosis or condition management: the makers describe it as a wellness app
use Android: the site links only to the App Store
want to compare prices before downloading: subscription prices are not listed on the website

pricing.intro: Pricing not published. PeakRoutine's website says it is free to start and that you can cancel a subscription any time from the app or the App Store, but it does not list prices.
notes: Check the App Store listing for current in-app prices.

alternatives.intro: Apps that also turn wearable data into coaching. Prices are as stated on each company's own site.

items.name: Bevel
items.what: AI health coach covering strain, sleep, recovery, nutrition and medical records
items.difference: Larger and more established, with its own strain and recovery scores and health-record storage; PeakRoutine centres on correlations between habits and six specialist coaches.

items.name: Welltory
items.what: HRV-based stress, energy and health tracking
items.difference: Built around HRV measurement and stress scores rather than habit plans.

items.name: Apple Health
items.difference: Collects the data PeakRoutine reads but does not explain correlations or coach you.

liked: Habits that adapt to how recovered you are, instead of punishing a missed day
Turning wearable data into something to act on
asked: Whether it gives a plan and daily goals rather than a short burst of motivation (yes, according to the maker)
Whether the six coaches are separate models (six custom models sharing one biomarker context, the team said)
How it avoids treating a coincidence as a pattern (the team said passive data alone can't fully separate two things that change together)
Whether it is for chronic conditions (no, it is a wellness app)

quotes.text: Finally an app that turns my wearable data into something I can actually act on instead of just staring at.
quotes.author: Zain Sheikh

quotes.text: Why would someone use this instead of Apple Health?
quotes.author: Aleksandar Blazhev

pros: Reads data from many wearables at once through Apple Health
Habit plans adjust to recovery rather than enforcing streaks
Says it never sells data or shares it with advertisers
cons: iPhone only, as far as its site shows
Prices are not published on its website
Not a medical tool, by the makers' own description

quotes.author: Aleksandar Blazhev
quotes.text: Why would someone use this instead of Apple Health?
quotes.reply: Siddhant Gupta said PeakRoutine is not trying to replace Apple Health but sits on top of it, with the dashboard, insights and habits all aimed at actually improving health.

quotes.author: Himani Sah
quotes.text: Is this more of a preventive care app or it's meant for people with chronic conditions or both?
quotes.reply: Priyank Tyagi replied that it is a wellness app at heart, not for diagnosing or managing a condition.

x.none: We found no posts about PeakRoutine on X yet.

faq.a: An iPhone app that connects your health data through Apple Health, finds patterns between sleep, HRV, daylight, exercise, nutrition and mood, and gives you six AI coaches and adaptive habit plans.
Its website says it is free to start and that subscriptions can be cancelled any time, but it does not publish prices. Check the App Store listing.

faq.q: Which wearables does PeakRoutine work with?
faq.a: Anything that syncs to Apple Health, such as Apple Watch, Oura or WHOOP, according to the maker.
No. The team describes it as a wellness app for day-to-day health and habits, not for diagnosing or managing conditions.
Its site says it never sells your data or shares it with advertisers, and that data is encrypted in transit and at rest.

faq.q: How is it different from Apple Health?
faq.a: It sits on top of Apple Health: Apple Health stores the data, PeakRoutine explains the links between it and coaches you on habits.
